source_integrity.summary: Revision 2 pending and English/Portuguese source blob hashes match producer-provided fingerprints 3/3. Revision 1 rejected record preserved; no approved or public report of this slug before publication.

schema_and_taxonomy.summary: Schema-v2 ready strategic-actors kind with political-economy-markets primary program, existing controlled taxonomy; biographical dossiers in existing public index use strategic-actors kind across political economy and global-system-power programs.

source_vintage_and_cutoff.summary: Historic events anchored to 1923 monetary reform, November 1932 petition, 1933 Reichsbank, 1934 MEFO device, 1 April 1938 issuance close, 1939 dispute and 1946 tribunal verdict; selected 1938/39–1944/45 nominal Reichsmark fiscal series explicitly dated, last year partly estimated.

factual_methodology.summary: Nuremberg tribunal records confirm 12 billion Reichsmarks in MEFO bills issued by 1 April 1938, invoice/guarantee/rediscount mechanics and Schacht's role; 1932 letter and petition participation documented in Yale/Harvard Nuremberg transcriptions and DHM biography; Bundesbank 2024 and IMF 2019 differ on 5% versus 4% paper rates, discrepancy explicitly acknowledged in both texts rather than presented as one universal rate; USHMM/IMT confirm acquittal on charged counts while preserving historical agency.

evidence_traceability.summary: 27 distinct citation URLs across 14 hosts shared in EN/PT. Prior rejected duplicate historical photograph citation corrected: [2] openly identified as photograph/editorial context and [15] now cites IMF research on clearing/New Plan. Primary tribunal, Bundesbank, IMF and academic economic history sampled for central finance and political claims. 1938–45 full historical fiscal charts reference table 4 of historical working paper; individual archival source rows not independently recompiled in this pass.

research_depth.summary: About 6006 EN and 7204 PT substantive words with 30 chapters and 30 numbered bibliography items, long-term biography, Rentenmark, anti-Nazi-to-Nazi institutional choices, MEFO credit, import controls, forced labour and recovery propaganda, Nuremberg judgment and postwar history.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Revision 1's decorative chronology charts replaced by three quantitative historical series with identical paired arrays: Mefo outstanding [11.9,11.4,10.8,10.1,9.5,8.8,8.1], nominal debt [53.2,73.5,102.6,153.3,208,284.9,387.9], notes/coins [11,15.2,18.3,23.8,29.8,38.7,73]. Same fiscal-year periods and caveats, 33 table rows, a map and a causal flow in both locales; monetary quantities are not combined as identical instruments.

bilingual_equivalence.summary: Same 3 chart arrays, 27 distinct URLs, historical agency claims, MEFO sources and rate discrepancy explicitly present in English and Portuguese; equivalent original-political agency attribution and conclusion.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: New 1932 petition narrative included in both languages, historic sources [2]/[15] correctly characterized, no prose written as instructions to the reader or site producer. Nuremberg legal verdict not misrepresented as total exoneration of historical conduct.

contrary_evidence.summary: DHM/Nuremberg evidence of political collaboration balanced with Tribunal legal acquittal; 4%-versus-5% source disagreement disclosed; aggregate 12bn issued does not equal outstanding fiscal stock or delivered military capacity.

counterfactual_review.summary: Distinct causal explanations for labour recovery, credit growth, price controls and rearmament; MEFO liquidity risks and external material constraints distinguished. Political and economic effects cannot be credited to one financier alone.

pipeline_validation.summary: Structural source checks reproduced: >1700 words each, 3 numerical charts, >=1 map, >=1 flow, >=3 table rows, >6 headings, >8 URLs on >=4 domains, exact EN/PT numerical equivalence. Final full npm build and site smoke verification require GitHub Actions.

limitations: Primary evidence checks were sampled from Nuremberg, Bundesbank, IMF, USHMM and published historical research, not a full reproduction of all financial series from original archives.
The 4% vs 5% quoted rate in different institutional sources is not silently resolved; original historical terms may vary by instrument and time.
No full Node repository checkout was executed for this source review; GitHub build checks required.
notes: Revision 2 supersedes previously rejected unpublished revision 1; producer's three specific blocking defects were checked for remediation, including 1932 agency, nondecorative finance charts and correct New Plan evidence. Do not publish if any source SHA changes.

producer_checks.source_check: Revised to address rejected v1 findings: added Deutsches Historisches Museum's 1932 petition chronology; replaced duplicated GHDI photographic citation for New Plan and bilateral clearing with IMF research; introduced financial time series from Burret, Feld and Köhler, table 4, with stocks, total debt and currency separately classified; differentiated 4% vs 5% coupon in sources; QA source-by-source review still required.

producer_checks.translation_parity: Both language editions have 31 H2 chapters, identical three chart datasets, financial periods and balances, parallel 1932 petition and revised clearing and source discussion.
